column1: # Functions in the Python and JVM bindings that may call the BLOCKING
# `with_ref()` — i.e. take the shell slot and wait behind a call parked on
# another thread. Read by scripts/check/c/snapshot-getters.sh, which fails on
# any caller not listed here AND on any row whose function no longer calls it.
# A row names a (file, function) pair; two classes in one file that share a
# method name (`srt/transport.rs` `socket_stats` on Sender and Receiver) are
#   blocking-op  the function is itself a blocking operation; waiting for the
#   needs-slot   a dynamic read of state that lives inside the shell, with no
#                meaningful answer while the slot is held. It waits for the
#                parked call to return; the language guides say so.
#   primitive    the registry method the other rows call.
# Not a candidate for this list — fix the function instead:
#   - a value that cannot change after construction (addresses, ports, stream
#     handles, URL text): capture it at construction, read `Owned::snapshot()`;
#     answer "held" without waiting (a parked call means open).
